meta.purpose: What a real food bank, pantry or free-meal programme gives a single adult with no money, how often, and on what conditions, by city.
meta.rule: confirmed=true only where the figure was read on the cited page or document itself (PDFs were text-extracted with pdftotext). confirmed=false means it came from a search-result summary or a secondary page and was not seen on the primary source. Nothing is estimated.
meta.general_caveat: In every city frequency and quantity are set pantry by pantry, not by the food bank network. The figures below are real published rules of named sites, not network-wide guarantees.

new_york_city.item: Emergency food providers may not require proof of need
new_york_city.figure: Persons receiving food must not be requested to: make a donation; pay for food; exchange services for food; participate in a religious or political activity; or, as a requirement to receive emergency food, provide documentation to prove their need.
new_york_city.note: Proposed 68 RCNY ch.4 'Emergency Food Assistance Program', s.4-03(m). Read in the proposed-rule text; adoption of the final text was not checked. Binds EFAP-funded pantries and soup kitchens (500+ citywide).

new_york_city.item: EFAP eligibility regardless of income or immigration status
new_york_city.figure: All New Yorkers eligible for emergency food regardless of income or immigration status
new_york_city.note: From a search-result summary of the HRA EFAP page; page not opened.

new_york_city.item: Pantry package size standard (NY State HPNAP, which funds NYC pantries)
new_york_city.figure: 3-day package = 9 meals (3 meals a day for 3 days). One-person household minimum: 5 vegetable/fruit choices, 3 protein choices, 2 dairy choices, 2 grain choices
new_york_city.publisher: New York State Department of Health, Hunger Prevention and Nutrition Assistance Program
new_york_city.note: A 'choice' is e.g. one 15 oz can of vegetables, one 15 oz can of beans, one quart of milk, one loaf of bread; 1 lb frozen meat = 4 protein choices. No pound weight is stated for the package.

new_york_city.item: NY Common Pantry (Manhattan, Food Bank For NYC network): visit frequency
new_york_city.note: 'Pantry packages are supplemental grocery packages ... proportional to the number of individuals in the family and provided every two weeks.' No pounds or meal count stated.

new_york_city.figure: ID for all adults in the household (state ID, IDNYC, or passport/ID from any country)
No income requirement; income is asked only to screen for SNAP, health insurance and rental assistance
All are welcomed regardless of immigration status

new_york_city.item: Food Bank For NYC (Harlem community pantry): conditions
new_york_city.figure: ID required; bring own bags/cart; appointment through the Plentiful app
new_york_city.note: Search-result summary of a third-party listing; not opened.

new_york_city.item: City Harvest Mobile Market: produce per person
new_york_city.figure: 3-4 lb of produce for one person per market date (35-50 lb for a family of five or more)
new_york_city.note: Search-result summary; City Harvest's own distribution page did not state amounts or ID rules. Requirements vary by market (some require ID and proof of address).

new_york_city.item: Holy Apostles Soup Kitchen (Chelsea): meal service
new_york_city.figure: Hot meals to-go, Monday-Friday, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM (one meal, weekdays only)
new_york_city.note: Meals per day not stated as a number; the single weekday service window implies one meal. Not open weekends.

new_york_city.figure: 'Everyone is welcome, without question or qualification.' No ID mentioned

los_angeles.item: LA Regional Food Bank TEFAP sites: income proof
los_angeles.figure: Proof of household income shall not be required; income eligibility is a self-declaration after reviewing posted guidelines; recipient signs the EFA-7 sign-in sheet
los_angeles.publisher: Los Angeles Regional Food Bank / California Department of Social Services
los_angeles.note: Clauses 4-5 of the TEFAP agency site agreement. 'Clients shall not be denied TEFAP food if they refuse to reveal any information that is not a requirement of TEFAP (e.g. demographics).' Free of charge; no donations may be requested.

los_angeles.figure: Food goes to eligible recipients who live in the site's defined service area; an out-of-area person is served once as a one-time exception and referred to their proper site
los_angeles.publisher: Los Angeles Regional Food Bank / CDSS

los_angeles.figure: Each site declares weekly, bi-weekly or monthly distribution
los_angeles.publisher: Los Angeles Regional Food Bank / CDSS
los_angeles.note: The agreement's schedule form; no network-wide per-person limit is set.

los_angeles.item: JFS LA SOVA pantry (LA Regional Food Bank partner): frequency
los_angeles.note: Income self-certified at or below 150% of the federal poverty level; West Hollywood residents need proof of address or an affidavit. Quantity per visit not stated.

los_angeles.item: A registered LA food bank pantry: frequency and documents
los_angeles.figure: Once a month with a food bank ID card; state ID, proof of address and income award letter at the first visit only
los_angeles.publisher: LA County Department of Mental Health resource list
los_angeles.note: Search-result summary of an old county list describing one pantry; not opened and dated. Do not treat as current LARFB policy.

los_angeles.figure: Three nutritious meals a day, available daily, to anyone who comes through the door
los_angeles.note: No ID requirement mentioned. A search summary adds '365 days a year' and 500-1,000 people per meal (not read on the page).

connecticut_new_haven.figure: Participants do not need to give their name or any form of I.D. and can attend any Mobile Pantry food truck site
connecticut_new_haven.publisher: Northeast District Department of Health (CT), explaining Connecticut Foodshare's Mobile Pantry

connecticut_new_haven.figure: Most sites open once every other week
connecticut_new_haven.note: Food may include several types of fresh produce, bread and frozen meat.

connecticut_new_haven.figure: The driver decides how much food each participant gets; the quantity can change every week

connecticut_new_haven.item: DESK (Downtown Evening Soup Kitchen, New Haven): meals
connecticut_new_haven.figure: One evening meal daily: Sun 2:30-3:00 pm (Chapel on the Green); Mon 5-6 pm; Tue-Thu 5-6 pm (Lower New Haven Green); Fri-Sat 4-5 pm at 84 Broadway
connecticut_new_haven.note: FAQ page gives evening meals Sun-Thu 5-6 pm; Friday/Saturday meals are at 84 Broadway (Yale Community Kitchen partnership per search summary).

connecticut_new_haven.figure: Grocery-style whole foods at 57 Olive St, every Wednesday 1:30-3:00 pm (FAQ says 2:00-3:00 pm)
connecticut_new_haven.note: Weekly; quantity per visit not published.

connecticut_new_haven.figure: No restrictions by residency status, citizenship or age; no 'proof' of need; a very short intake form (meals: optional monthly demographics; pantry: brief paperwork annually)

london.figure: You need to be referred for a food voucher; the voucher is exchanged at the food bank for a food parcel
london.note: Referrers are frontline agencies (Citizens Advice, GPs, housing officers, schools, social workers). Westminster Chapel food bank: 'All clients must be referred by one of our Registered Agencies', appointments only, Westminster residents.

london.figure: An emergency food parcel containing at least three days of meals
london.note: Westminster Chapel (Trussell network, London) says 'three days'-worth of nutritionally balanced (non-perishable) food' (https://westminsterchapel.org.uk/foodbank/, confirmed). Citizens Advice: 'Your parcel will usually contain enough food for 3 days' (confirmed).

london.figure: 'Foodbanks in our network work on a three-voucher guideline, not a rule or restriction. If someone is referred to a foodbank more than three times in six months, it is flagged on the system so the foodbank can talk to the referral agency.'
london.publisher: Cardiff Foodbank (Trussell network), hosted on trussell.org.uk
london.note: Same handbook: food 'should last three days at least'; a second voucher within three days only in exceptional circumstances. The flag is a prompt, not a cap.

london.figure: 'There is no limit to the number of referrals you can make - so long as the person is in genuine need and IS receiving AND engaging in support to get them out of crisis.'
london.publisher: Abergele & District food bank (Trussell network), hosted on trussell.org.uk
london.note: Under 'Step 4 - More than 3 in 6 months'. Also: referrals two consecutive weeks or more get a reduced shopping list (items lasting more than a week are left out). A single food bank, Wales; shows the current network practice, not a London figure.

london.figure: Up to 6 vouchers in six months; each voucher used once; must have a voucher before collecting
london.note: A real London local cap, double the three-voucher guideline.

london.item: Older wording of the three-in-six-months guideline
london.figure: 'You might only receive three vouchers in six months unless there are exceptional circumstances'
london.note: Search summary only. No 2024-2026 network-wide change to a formal limit was found; the change is in framing (guideline/flag, 'no limit' if engaging with support) and local caps (Isle of Wight: max 3 vouchers in 6 months, per search summary; Lewisham: 6 in 6 months, confirmed).

london.item: Hackney Foodbank (Hackney, Newham, Tower Hamlets): referral
london.figure: Voucher code referral system issued by local agencies
london.note: No visit cap stated on the page.

dublin.item: Capuchin Day Centre (Bow Street): opening and meals
dublin.figure: Open Monday to Saturday including bank holidays; breakfast 7:30-11:30 am, lunch 12:30-3:00 pm (two meals a day, six days)
dublin.note: About 350 at breakfast and 700 at dinner daily; over 1,400 food parcels a week. Closed Sundays.

dublin.figure: Guests are served on a 'no questions asked' basis

dublin.item: Capuchin Day Centre: weekly food parcels
dublin.figure: Over 700 meals each day and over 1,500 food parcels each Wednesday
dublin.note: Parcel day is Wednesday. Irish Times reporting (search summary, not opened): parcels from about 7:30 am to anyone who turns up, containing tea, sugar, bread, tinned stew, soup, cheese, butter, meat and jam.

dublin.figure: Emergency food via a 'food collection & casework service' (Finglas, Jobstown, Portland Row) giving non-perishable food; contact food@crosscare.ie / 01-8913022. Portland Café serves breakfast and lunch from 8 am Mon-Fri
dublin.note: Frequency, parcel size and café prices not published. Funded through the EU ESF+ programme.

dublin.item: Society of St Vincent de Paul: how help comes
dublin.figure: Two trained volunteers arrange a home visit; SVP is not an emergency service and visits may take up to two weeks after contact
dublin.publisher: Society of St Vincent de Paul Ireland
dublin.note: Help is practical or financial aid with essentials; food vouchers are cited in search summaries but not on this page.

toronto.item: Daily Bread member food banks: frequency
toronto.figure: One Daily Bread member food bank once per week
2 to 3 days' worth of food, based on household size
No ID is required for a single person; ID needed only to register other household members. Intake asks name, address and date of birth
toronto.note: Some member food banks have catchment areas; outside them you may be referred elsewhere.

toronto.item: North York Harvest (Oriole Food Space): documents
toronto.figure: Proof of address (a piece of mail) and identification; appointments, no walk-ins; first-time clients register by phone
toronto.note: Search-result summary; North York Harvest's own get-food page returned 404. Visit frequency not found.

vancouver.figure: Once a week at any one distribution location, following the schedule
vancouver.note: A 211 BC listing (search summary, not opened) says distribution excludes the week provincial income-assistance cheques are issued.

vancouver.figure: 10-15 fresh, non-perishable or frozen food items weekly
vancouver.note: Dairy, proteins, vegetables, pasta, canned goods; monthly extra packs for children under 12 and seniors 65+.

vancouver.figure: Appointment only (604-876-3601); government-issued photo ID for every adult 18+; proof of address dated within 3 months in Vancouver, Burnaby, New Westminster or the North Shore
vancouver.note: No walk-in registration. A person with no address cannot meet the proof-of-address rule as written.

mexico_city.note: Programme 'Comedores para el Bienestar' run by SEBIEN. Government adds a MXN 13 subsidy per ración. 543 sites across 16 alcaldías; 25 million raciones planned for 2026. sebien.cdmx.gob.mx refused connection, so read via Infobae.

mexico_city.item: Comedores Comunitarios: hours and meals a day
mexico_city.figure: Monday-Friday, 13:00-16:00; one comida (midday meal) a day
mexico_city.note: Hours may be adjusted at the community's request. Not open weekends.

mexico_city.figure: Free; 10:00-17:00 or until the raciones run out
mexico_city.note: Priority to children, older people and people with disabilities.

mexico_city.item: Comedores: who may eat and documents
mexico_city.figure: Anyone; write full name, sex, age and signature in the attendance book; no ID or proof of address requested
mexico_city.note: 'Nadie que transite o habite la ciudad queda excluido por su condición económica o lugar de origen.'

mexico_city.item: Alimento para Todos IAP (Central de Abasto, CDMX food bank): despensa
mexico_city.figure: 30 kg of product for at most MXN 300; always includes rice, beans and 1 kg of tortillas; weekly, to 125,000+ families
mexico_city.note: Distribution is through organized communities that collect by truck and pay per quantity distributed, not to walk-in individuals. Its comedor at the Central de Abasto sells a complete meal for MXN 16 to market workers.

mexico_city.item: Alimento para Todos: cuota de recuperación share
mexico_city.figure: Recovery fee of at most 10% of the price
mexico_city.note: Same article: 25,000 families / 116,000 people a month (a different count from La Silla Rota's weekly figure).

mexico_city.item: Banco de Alimentos (Cáritas/BAMX) Iztapalapa: individual eligibility
mexico_city.figure: Adult head of household, income at most MXN 3,800 a month (or minimum pension), not a business owner; first-timers register with Trabajo Social at Maíz 180, Bodega 3, Granjas Esmeralda, Iztapalapa, Mon-Fri 12:30-15:30
mexico_city.note: Cuota amount, frequency and contents not stated. Individuals can apply directly here, subject to social-work intake.

mexico_city.item: BAMX network cuota de recuperación (outside CDMX, for reference)
mexico_city.figure: 15-20% of the real value of the package; packages every 15 days
mexico_city.note: Banco de Alimentos Cáritas Aguascalientes, not CDMX. Shows the BAMX model: a small payment, fortnightly.

mexico_city.item: Uniendo Manos sponsorship (Banco de Alimentos, Guadalajara)
mexico_city.figure: Sponsor pays the cuota so a family receives two despensas a month
mexico_city.note: Jalisco, not CDMX; confirms despensas are normally paid for and twice-monthly in the BAMX model.

meal_equivalency.figure: A meal from Feeding America is 1.2 pounds of product, based on USDA guidelines
meal_equivalency.note: Footnote to FY2025 (2024-07-01 to 2025-06-30) figures. feedingamerica.org/ways-to-give/faq/about-our-claims also says 'Each meal is roughly 1.2 pounds' (confirmed).

meal_equivalency.item: Pounds per day and per 3-day supply
meal_equivalency.figure: 1.2 lb x 3 meals = 3.6 lb per day; 3 days' food for 1 person = 10.8 lb; 5 days = 18 lb; 7 days = 25.2 lb
meal_equivalency.note: Arithmetic from the 1.2 lb standard, published by the agency.

meal_equivalency.figure: At least three days of meals
meal_equivalency.note: Trussell's own pages give days, not a meal count. A count of nine meals (3 x 3) would be inference, not a Trussell figure; none found on a Trussell page.

not_found: A Food Bank For NYC or City Harvest network-wide rule on visit frequency (set by each pantry).
Pounds per pantry visit for any NYC, LA or New Haven pantry (only CT Foodshare's 'driver decides' and the HPNAP 9-meal standard).
An LA Regional Food Bank network-wide frequency rule; its own Find Food page publishes none.
A Trussell network-wide formal change to the three-in-six-months guideline in 2024-2026 (only the 'no limit if engaging with support' wording and local caps).
North York Harvest visit frequency (its page 404'd).
Crosscare and SVP parcel size and frequency; Capuchin parcel contents on a primary page.
The cuota amount in pesos for an individual's despensa at a CDMX food bank.
